title: Tanzanian Amaranth Greens
community: Enjoyed nationwide — one of Tanzania's most important vegetables
author: Mama Salima
desc: Tanzanian Mchicha — amaranth leaves sautéed with onions, tomatoes, and garlic until wilted and richly flavoured. Tanzania's most nutritious everyday green — more iron and protein than spinach, widely grown and deeply beloved.
longDesc: Mchicha (amaranth) is Tanzania's most important leafy vegetable — more nutritious than spinach, incredibly fast to cook, and available at every market. It is the green that accompanies ugali at the majority of Tanzanian family meals. Its preparation is simple but the result is deeply satisfying.
ingredients: 500g fresh mchicha (amaranth leaves) — washed and roughly chopped
steps: Add garlic and curry powder. Stir 30 seconds.
Add tomatoes. Cook 5 minutes until softened.
Cover and cook 4—5 minutes until completely wilted.
Season with salt and pepper. Serve immediately.
chefTips: Do not add water — the leaves release plenty of moisture.
Brief cooking preserves the bright green colour and nutrients.
Mchicha wilts dramatically — 500g raw produces a modest serving.
cookingScience: Amaranth leaves contain oxalic acid which dissolves in the water released during cooking — brief cooking minimises oxalic acid buildup in the cooking liquid. The iron in mchicha is non-haem iron; pairing with the tomato's vitamin C significantly increases its absorption.
sustainabilityTips: Mchicha grows rapidly with minimal water — one of Tanzania's most sustainable crops.
healthBenefits: Complete plant protein when combined with beans.
culturalNote: Mchicha is Tanzania's most democratic vegetable — grown in virtually every household garden, bought at every market, and eaten by every family regardless of income. It is the green that has nourished Tanzania for generations.
